svg.text: ANTIBACTERIALS — FOUR QUESTIONS BEFORE YOU GIVE ONE
Not which drug is strongest, but which drug fits this organism, this patient, this site.

g.text: Most sore throats, colds, coughs and
watery diarrhoea are viral. An antibiotic
will not shorten them by a single day.
Bactericidal drugs kill outright and are
needed when the immune system cannot
A drug that never crosses into the brain,
the bone or the urine is useless there,
kidney or liver disease, or a genuine
allergy. Each rules some drugs out.

svg.text: DRUGS WITH A NAME THAT WARNS YOU

g.text: Aminoglycosides such as gentamicin — damage hearing and kidneys. Levels and creatinine are checked.
Tetracyclines — stain developing teeth, so avoided in pregnancy and in young children.
Chloramphenicol — can destroy the bone marrow. Reserved, never casual.

svg.text: FINISH THE COURSE THAT WAS PRESCRIBED — AND PRESCRIBE A SHORT ONE

g.text: Feeling better on day three does not mean cured. Stopping early leaves the toughest organisms alive.

svg.text: Every antibiotic given today makes the next one work a little less well. That is the cost you are spending.
